messages:
maria: Heads-up — hit a flaky parsing bug in the onboarding sample app streaming path. When reconnects happen we sometimes end up missing or duplicating the tail fragment of a JSON payload, which leaves the client parser hung. Repro below.

ben: is this EventSource in the browser or fetch streams in node? tiny repro please.

maria: both. EventSource in browser sample and node-fetch in the node sample. Steps: 1) start a stream that emits multi-chunk JSON logical messages 2) simulate network flap midway through a message 3) client resumes with Last-Event-ID but receives parts that lead to duplicate or missing pieces.

sam: do you have a console trace or server logs for the reconnect window? might be a resume-token semantics mismatch.

maria: client console snippet: 

received chunk: {\"id\":1,\"data\":\"{\\\"text\\\":\\\"Hello\\\"}\"}
received chunk: {\"id\":2,\"data\":\"{\\\"text\\\":\\\"Wo\\\"}\"}
// network drops here
reconnect with Last-Event-ID: 2
received chunk: {\"id\":2,\"data\":\"rld\\\"}\nreceived chunk: {\"id\":3,\"data\":\"{\\\"text\\\":\\\"Bye\\\"}\"}

maria: result: sometimes the \"rld\" fragment arrives as a separate resent fragment, causing the client to assemble id 2 twice or interleave fragments with id 3. Parser then errors or produces duplicated substrings.

ben: that suggests Last-Event-ID is being advanced at fragment emission rather than at full logical message flush. We should not treat chunk emission as atomic event boundary for resume.

sam: on the runtime we currently emit fragments as they complete at the tokenizer/kernel layer. We could add an explicit logical-boundary sentinel (e.g., a comment line `: boundary <token>` when a full logical message is complete) so clients can resume idempotently.

maria: that would be ideal. Currently SDK parity is rough — python sample waits for newline termination, go sample tries to parse each chunk which explains why go/mobile sees worse behavior.

ben: immediate mitigation: add defensive reassembly in the sample apps. Store last-seen fragment hash per event id and drop duplicates on resume. Ugly but low-risk until server framing is changed. Also add a short note in the quickstart telling users to use the helper.

maria: working on a patch: 1) browser sample gets an event-id buffer + dedupe, 2) node sample adds same helper, 3) added headless test harness that toggles network to reproduce.

sam: please also file a runtime ticket to normalize resume semantics; include the server logs and client traces. We need a plan: either server-side atomic flush or a durable resume token that maps to logical messages, not raw fragments.

maria: filed TKT-3412: \"streaming: make resume tokens map to logical message boundaries; avoid advancing token on fragment emission\" with attached traces.

ben: quick review of the PR — looks good. Add an inline comment explaining the fragment-hash dedupe hack so future maintainers understand the context.

maria: added the comment and README entry in sample-app/STREAMING.md describing the SDK differences and the temporary workaround. Pushed.

deploy-bot: deploy queued: sample-app/dev -> staging (job 7843) :rocket:

ben: once runtime has an ETA we should update SDKs and remove the workaround. Also consider adding a small interop test matrix across node/python/go/mobile in CI.

sam: agreed. Created follow-up TKT-3417 to add cross-SDK streaming interop tests.

maria: thanks — marking this thread for follow-up when runtime change lands. :thumbsup:
